audit_findings.title: The operating joint venture may be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $160.1m bridge addition, equal to $5.13 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: JV earnings may remain in OE while the $160.1m JV investment is also added through the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: Our investment in the Joint Venture is accounted for using the equity method of accounting, and those results have been included for the same period as our March 31 fiscal year end.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing OE reconciliation leaves the double count unresolved rather than demonstrated. Even if the entire $160.1m bridge addition were removed, bear, base, and bull values would decline to approximately $134.11, $174.66, and $204.73 per share. Base value would remain below the $194.48 market price, bull value would remain above it, and the buy-below conclusion would remain far below market.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year to equity-method earnings. If those earnings remain in OE, rerun all scenarios without the $160.1m stake addition; otherwise document the annual purges.

audit_findings.title: The FY2026 anchor contains only a partial year of the new note interest
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.4m pretax recurring shortfall, computed as the $37.5m annual coupon less $14.1m recognized; approximately $18.3m after the filed 21.8% tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: The unnormalized OE anchor omits part of the recurring interest charge retained under the equity-level OE method
audit_findings.evidence: The increase was mainly due to increased interest expense of approximately $14.1 million on our 5.000% Senior Unsecured Notes due May 2036, which were issued on November 13, 2025; $1.9 million of higher interest on our Term Loan, which was increased to $300.0 million in February 2025; and $0.4 million of increased debt amortization costs related to these new borrowings, all of which were partially offset by approximately $4.4 million of increased interest income resulting from a higher cash balance and higher Interest Capitalized of approximately $6.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch: the $750m notes carry a $37.5m annual coupon but contributed only $14.1m to FY2026 interest expense. Applying the resulting $18.3m after-tax reduction proportionally to the supplied DCF lowers value by approximately $6.24, $8.24, and $9.72 per share in the bear, base, and bull cases. The bull premium over the $194.48 price falls from $15.38 to about $5.66, making the omission reasonably capable of changing the investment interpretation.
audit_findings.action: Normalize forecast OE for a full year of note interest and issuance-cost amortization, exclude separately purged interest income from the offset, and rerun every scenario and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may escape the equity-level OE charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.819m in FY2026 and $3.822m in Q1 FY2027; omitted portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized cash interest may be absent from current OE and also absent from reinvestment if growth-project capex was excluded
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in Interest Capitalized was due primarily to capital spending for the expansion and modernization of our cement plant in Laramie, Wyoming and our gypsum wallboard plant in Oklahoma.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate substantial capitalized interest, but the supplied record does not show whether it was included in project spending, another OE deduction, or neither. The issue therefore remains a possible omission whose valuation materiality cannot be established from the available OE workpaper.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized interest by project and year through cash capex and the OE calculation, deduct it exactly once, and rerun the valuation if any amount escaped both OE and reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: Known project spending may exceed the DCF's generic reinvestment allowance
audit_findings.magnitude: $490m-$525m expected FY2027 capex; after $120.755m spent in Q1, $369.245m-$404.245m remains within the annual guidance
audit_findings.mechanism: Known project outlays may be omitted from forecast reinvestment while generic growth is applied to OE
audit_findings.evidence: Capital expenditures for fiscal 2027 are expected to range from $490.0 million to $525.0 million and to be allocated between the Heavy Materials and Light Materials sectors.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed FY2027 spending range exceeds the $371.4m OE anchor and includes two unfinished expansion projects, while the valuation has no separate perimeter adjustment. Although the filing does not split maintenance from growth spending, the remaining outlay is large enough to change value materially if it is not captured before incremental project earnings are credited.
audit_findings.action: Build a year-by-year reconciliation of remaining Laramie and Duke project spending, maintenance capex, and other capex against modeled reinvestment; then rerun cash flows with project earnings beginning only when the associated capacity becomes operational.

audit_findings.title: Mining reclamation obligations are not visible in the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncaptured reclamation or closure costs would reduce OE when accrued or settled, or require a liability deduction in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: We are contingently liable for performance under $48.7 million in performance bonds relating primarily to our mining operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing reports $52.2m of performance bonds, but that amount is security for performance rather than the underlying reclamation liability and cannot be deducted mechanically. Other long-term liabilities were $68.236m, yet the record does not identify the reclamation component or show whether recurring accruals are already in OE. Materiality therefore cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the asset-retirement and reclamation liability roll-forward, expected settlement schedule, and related expense accounts; confirm each obligation is captured once in OE or the bridge and rerun if a material uncovered amount exists.

audit_findings.title: Nonoperating and potentially nonroutine income may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: up to the $5.108m FY2026 pretax balance; approximately $1.80 per share of base-value impact if the entire balance were removed after the filed 21.8% tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonroutine asset sales or duplicated investment income would inflate normalized OE
audit_findings.evidence: Other Nonoperating Income consists of a variety of items that are not related to segment operations, including lease and rental income, investment income, asset sales, and other miscellaneous income and cost items, such as large non-routine sales of excess raw materials or energy.
audit_findings.explanation: The exact nonroutine component is unresolved, but the entire FY2026 balance is only 1.4% of the $371.4m anchor. Even the conservative assumption that all $5.108m is nonrecurring produces an estimated base-value reduction of only about $1.80 per share, versus the $14.69 gap between base value and the $194.48 market price, so it cannot change the stated valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2026 account-level composition, remove asset sales, large nonroutine items, and investment income represented by separately added assets, and document the adjustment without otherwise changing valuation inputs.
